facts.text: I have pain in my heel.
The pain is most intense in my right heel.
It came on gradually over the past 2 weeks.

facts.item: heel pain: injury that started it
facts.text: Not particularly. I can't recall anything where I might have injured my heel.
It's intermittent.
It usually happens every day.
It seems to be worse in the morning. It hurts most first thing in the morning or at the end of the day.

facts.item: heel pain: change since it started
facts.text: It has stayed about the same.
When it hurts, it can get up to a 7 out of 10.
Sometimes it extends into the arch of my foot.

facts.item: heel pain: spread up the leg
facts.text: It doesn't spread up my leg.

facts.item: heel pain: what it feels like
facts.text: It's a stretching, tearing pain.

facts.item: heel pain: what makes it better
value: massaging the arch of the foot
facts.text: Massaging the arch of my foot and applying ice make it better.

facts.item: heel pain: how much treatment helps
facts.text: I've used ice, massage and occasional ibuprofen for the pain, but they give me only limited relief.

facts.item: heel pain: what makes it worse
value: walking after sitting for a long time
facts.text: Walking barefoot, or walking after sitting for a long period of time, makes it worse.

other_considerations.note: Causes posterior heel pain from irritation of the bursae around the Achilles insertion, often from ill-fitting footwear or a Haglund deformity.
Tibial nerve compression at the medial heel causes pain, burning, tingling, or numbness radiating to the plantar heel and sole.
Look for an entrance wound and signs of local infection; the patient may not describe a mechanism of injury.
Usually follows rolling the ankle, with ligament tenderness, laxity, edema, and ecchymosis.

source_issues: Heart rate disagrees: doorway HR 69/minute vs patient-note exam HR 72 beats per minute (e004). Doorway value kept as heart rate (x004); the note value is 'heart rate on recheck' (x005).
Exam lines e006 ('Extremities:') and e012 ('Neuro:') are bare section headers split off by the parser; listed in excluded_exam_lines.

Exam lines e010, e011, and e015 do not state the side; the SP notes and history place the findings on the right foot. Kept as written, with the SP-simulated right-foot findings added to the same records (x013, x014).
The note HPI says ice, massage, and occasional ibuprofen gave 'limited relief' (note fact f014); the script says massage and ice make the pain better (p012, f013).

The note FH says the patient denies a family history of rheumatologic disorders, while the father has arthritis (p021, type not given). The family rheumatologic denial was not added as a patient fact.

Gold rank 1 lists exam findings (tenderness over the medial calcaneal tuberosity, pain with toe dorsiflexion) under history findings. Its 'first few steps in the morning' is not in the script, which says the pain is worse in the morning and after prolonged sitting; 'first few steps after sitting' comes from the SP notes.
Gold rank 2 'Diffuse pain over heel' is not supported by the script (pain most intense in the right heel), and 'Refractory to conservative management' rests only on the note's 'limited relief'.
Raw sheet artifact: part of the Foreign body / Ankle sprain rationale text is pasted into the examinee checklist after 'Entrance'. Parsed fields are not affected.
The note exam reports a nonantalgic gait, while the SP is told to show pain with the first few steps after sitting; not necessarily a contradiction, and both are in the gait record (x018).
notes: p005 and p006 both answer when the pain is worse; merged into one time-of-day fact (f007). 'Usually every day' (p005) is the frequency child f006.
Training for a marathon (p003) and being a runner (p023) say different things: f037 (exercise) with the marathon training as its child f038 (v1 f004, social, mapped to habit_exposure).

Note-only facts (v1 from_note): no proximal radiation (f011), limited relief of conservative measures (f014), PMH denials of cancer, rheumatologic disorders, and diabetes (f028-f030), and family denials of cancer and diabetes (f035-f036).
Daily intermittent heel pain is the ongoing presenting problem, so its attributes are marked current rather than recurrent.

SP-simulated findings: pain on toe extension goes into the toe dorsiflexion record (x014), pain on palpation of the arch and plantar heel into the heel and foot palpation record (x013), and pain with the first few steps after sitting into the gait record (x018), because it is elicited when the examinee watches him walk.

Conversion: the relieving list (f013) is not marked complete, because the note adds occasional ibuprofen (f014). The radiation list (f010) is complete; the note's denial of proximal radiation (f011) agrees.
Conversion: alcohol (p024) is a parent (f039) with a quantity child (f040).
Vitals: doorway values agree with the note's 'VS: WNL' (e002), so each doorway record cites both; the note's different heart rate (72) is a separate recheck record (x005), not initial.
Harmonisation pass: scale [0, 10] added to f009.
Fixes: f039 answer word removed; f045 new fact 'marital status' from f043.
